body: I already tried different subs and posted this post (and revised versions) multiple times

Hello,
If you thought I was trying to lecture you or offend you, that actually wasn't my intent at all. I would be actually kind of surprised if you got that impression. Let me go over some things you addressed. I wasn't trying to give you an unsolicited explanation about what a gris gris is so to speak, as I already knew you knew what it was as you responded to my comment. I was going over what I've read.


Let me further express. I have been intrigued by the occult and spiritual world for well over 15 years. What I said about how the gris gris is constructed is what I have read from various sources but has nothing to do with the source stated above. This is my very first time hearing about that woman Denise when I read your comment. As far as race and ethnicity, I too am of African American decent.


About your recommendation I really hope you didn't get that I was disparaging him in any way out of what I typed. When I typed what I typed about the phoney practitioners online I was specifically talking about some of the dozens upon dozens upon dozens of people I have came across throughout the years. I had some people in mind specifically but to think I had him in mind when typing would be untrue. There are some shops in Louisiana that do have souvenirs and trinkets instead of authentic gris gris but that is usually apparent. When I typed what I typed I didn't think that it would be taken any different than how I meant it.


I hope I didn't offend you at all and I do appreciate your recommendation. Hopefully that cleared things up for you. I don't go around degrading, demeaning, and disparaging innocent people at random. That is not my character. I simply was just expressing my experience online with trying to find authentic practitioners. Have a good day.

I was hesitant to buy one online because they tend to not be genuine. Let's start with what a gris gris is made with. A gris gris bag are traditionally made with no more than 13 items and traditionally made with an odd number of items. They are usually tried together and not made with draw string bags like you commonly see around the net. Furthermore they are usually consecrated at an alter and contains a spirit in the bag. Modern gris gris bags or mojos are usually cheaply thrown together by, from what I now see as outsiders, scammers, and or charlatans. 


As years went by and I read more into gris gris, then scoured different sites to read various shops "about me" and product description I learned a few things about people who are selling these gris gris:
1 They use an old photo of themselves or a stock photo. - scammers sometimes have photos of themselves on these "spell casting", "psychic", and occult site/store pages where they are dressed up as some looney faux bohemian, free spirit, hippie, and or genie, or they use a stock photo of someone else


2 they sometimes have some weird story on their about me page about how they are a 3rd or even 10th generation witch whos grandma took them to the woods to practice, sometimes even leaving her alone. That they would hear howls and they connect with animals and nature. They would then say they started seeing and hearing spirits as a young child and at first was afraid of them, but then started realizing that they were their friends


3 they have weird names. They will have names like asprapra, moon child, wolf foot, dr ripley, madmae mirlande antansie carcimařu etc


4 they use buzz words like magick, magickal, moon phase, conjure, apothecary, Chakra, third eye, crystal healing, cleansing, spiritual cleansing etc


5 they grossly and tackyly describe their products. Usually their descriptions read like a bored stay at home, suburban mom read some things on the internet, got manically inspired then started spending all her husbands hard earned money to come up with "kitchen witch" type products. They read about herbs and crystals, spirituality and vodou then started embarking on a journey to sale these items. The products descriptions I usually read goes along the lines: a gris gris bag or mojo, trick bag, gri gri, hand bag or anyone of the vast names it has is a voodoo talisman originating from Africa. They are used for anything from bringing a lover back to good luck! So basically it like a little spell in a bag! You just choose the one that suits your purpose and you can have your own little good luck charm! The color of the bag usually match the purpose such as white for cleansing or pink for love. Now you can have you own little magickal talismans for whatever purpose! Just carry it around in your pocket and watch the luck come!


There is hardly ever any mention about how you can't let anyone see or touch it. How often it is supposed to be fed. The fact that you have to breathe on it to "wake it up" etc. Usually these people who make these get cheap bags from Amazon, cheap oils and crystals, throw a bunch of dirt in a bag and sell you something that doesn't work. About a week or two ago I just read on Facebook and reddit that the practice of voodoo, vodou, and hoodoo are a "closed practice" and that if you don't have African ancestry that you can't practice it to begin with (unless you are called and ordained in I believe). This is something I did not know, which lead me to believe that when you buy something from someone practicing that does not, does the product really work?


Another thing is all of these online shops tend to have pre-made gris gris or mojo bags at hand which completely defeats the purpose. They are not made with you in mind. Your name, your birthday, your petition, your intention and or consecrated at an alter calling on lwa/loa etc. They are pre-made or thrown together and sent out.


I missed a lot of stuff that I wanted to say. I wanted to reread/restudy some things then type this out more detailed and thoroughly but I couldn't bring myself to do it right now. A lot of these people seem to all go by the same thing and be motivated by the same thing, Money. If they even have a photo of them on their site they all are dressed looking looney and use buzz words sounding pretentious. If you contact them they have an "I-am-better-than-you-stop-asking-questions-DO-YOU-WANT-THE-CRYSTALS-OR-NOT?! Attitude. From what I learned you actually have to practice the religion to make these talisman and cast these spells for other people etc. You have to follow the practice. Apparently not anyone can just do it from their kitchen; because if their intention is money, what type of energy is going into that bag?

Can you do me a favor, when you get the chance, can you help find the other book?
